source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus, three buildings coded NVA5 through NVA7 at a single Pacific Boulevard address, publishes 116 MW of IT capacity across roughly 1.18 million square feet of technical space. That is the largest single published figure among the five Virginia facilities on this site that have reported a megawatt number at all, out of 326 mapped facilities in the state, and it accounts for just under half of the 233 MW total this site has collected from Virginia operator spec pages. No certifications are listed on the operator's spec page, so no inference about qualifying workloads can be drawn from that category.

The 116 MW figure is IT load, meaning power delivered to the equipment, not facility gross draw. At 40 kW per rack, a common assumption for AI training density, 116 MW would support roughly 2,900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a common assumption for mixed enterprise load, the same power would support roughly 11,600 racks. The arithmetic is 116,000 kW divided by the assumed rack density. CyrusOne publishes neither rack count nor a target density, so neither figure is the operator's claim.

Virginia's Northern Virginia corridor is the densest data center market in the United States by most industry measures, and Sterling sits within it, but this site holds no state-context data on grid constraints, utility relationships, or power availability specific to this campus. The absence of published certifications means this site cannot characterize what regulated or sensitive workloads the campus is qualified to host. A reader evaluating AI relevance should treat 116 MW as a meaningful floor on capacity, treat the rack translations above as illustrative arithmetic only, and seek operator or utility disclosures not reproduced here for anything beyond those published facts.
